4. Mr.Shalin Mehta learned Senior Advocate assisted by Mr.G.H.Upadhyay learned advocate for the appellant made the following submissions:
4.1 Mr.Mehta would submit that it is well settled that the provisions of Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure are not applicable to a land reference case under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act.

Inviting our attention to the provisions of Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, Mr.Mehta would submit that when the amount of compensation has been NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3107/2024 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined settled under Section 11 as is the case on hand i.e. when undisputedly at the stage of Section 4, Section 6 and Section 11 it was apparent that the appellants' names were on record of the notices and the award.
The question of payment of compensation was already settled and there was no case for deciding as to which person would receive compensation.

4.2 Mr.Mehta would submit that based on the Revenue Entry No.940 dated 28.04.1970 on which basis a certificate was issued in the name of Magan Mangal,
Mohan Mangal, Shankar Mangal and Chhagan Mangal, it was undisputed that they are from the 'Parmar' family.

4.3 Mr.Mehta would further submit that the very fact that post the death of Shankar Magnal Gohil in the year 1993, the exercise of heir-ship NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3107/2024 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined entry was carried out in the year 1997 for lands except the land in question being survey no.335,
the presumption therefore is clear that this land belonged to the Parmar Branch and not the Gohil branch.
4.4

Revenue Entry No.1582.

Even in absence of any challenge to the order of the Deputy Collector dated 09.03.2013 in RTS Appeal No.80 of 2009, cancelling this Revenue Entry as no other directions were issued by the Deputy Collector, the award under Section 11 would entitle the appellants for compensation.

4.6 Mr.Mehta would submit by reading Section 13 of the Land Acquisition Act that the Collector can only correct any clerical or arithmetical mistake in the award and nothing beyond that is permissible.

4.7 He would further submit that the reference under Section 18 was only filed by Pratapbhai Maganbhai Gohil for enhancement of compensation and no dispute was raised as to the entitlement of who is the correct claimant.
Reading Section 30 of the Act would submit that the Reference Court has power to settle the dispute only between parties to the award.

By the order under challenge, the Reference Court NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3107/2024 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined has decided the title of the parties in a way by declaring that Mangal Natha was the owner of the land, the land was never granted in his name.

The question as to whether Shankar Mangal and Chhagan Mangal belong to Parmar Family or to Gohil Family is a matter of jurisdiction of Civil Court and no competent Court has declared that the appellants are not the interested persons.

4.8 Mr.Mehta would submit that when there is voluminous evidence in the form of Section 4, Section 6 notifications and the award under Section 11 which indicated the names of the appellants, the Trial Court had not given any reasons why these evidences produced by the appellants be ignored.

The opinion of the Trial Court in concluding that cancellation of the Revenue entry no.1582 was conclusive evidence, is not sufficient as it is settled law that Revenue NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3107/2024 CAV JUDGMENT DATED: 30/09/2024 undefined Entries are only for fiscal purposes and do not decide the rights of the parties.
4.9 He would further submit that individuals cannot be added by Order 1 Rule 10 in the Reference proceedings.
In support of his submission, he will rely on the decision in the case of Smt. Ambey Devi v. State of Bihar and another reported in AIR 1996 SC 1513.
